description: The bar chart illustrates the “Bias Percentage” across two domains — Sports and Healthcare — under three contact conditions (“No Contact,” “Positive Contact,” and “Negative Contact”) both “Before” and “After” an intervention, as evaluated in the paper “Breaking Bias, Building Bridges: Evaluation and Mitigation of Social Biases in LLMs via Contact Hypothesis.” The vertical axis represents Bias Percentage, ranging from 0 to 70 in increments of 10. Each domain (Sports and Healthcare) contains three grouped bars, each subdivided into “Before” and “After” segments, with distinct patterns and colors indicating contact type: gray for “No Contact,” red for “Positive Contact,” and blue for “Negative Contact,” with hatched patterns denoting the “After” condition. In Sports, “No Contact Before” shows 45.42% bias, rising slightly to 45.42 + 7.45 = 52.87% after; “Positive Contact Before” is 43.65%, increasing to 43.65 + 8.31 = 51.96% after; “Negative Contact Before” is 50.05%, rising to 50.05 + 8.33 = 58.38% after. In Healthcare, “No Contact Before” is 38.08%, unchanged after (0.00 added); “Positive Contact Before” is 35.38%, increasing slightly to 35.39 after (0.01 added); “Negative Contact Before” is 40.79%, unchanged after (0.00 added). For the second Healthcare group, “No Contact Before” is 40.70%, unchanged after; “Positive Contact Before” is 37.51%, increasing to 37.52 after (0.01 added); “Negative Contact Before” is 46.73%, increasing to 46.84 after (0.11 added). The chart visually suggests that while some contact conditions slightly reduce bias (e.g., Positive Contact in Healthcare), others — particularly Negative Contact — tend to increase or maintain high bias levels, especially in Sports. The “After” segments are consistently smaller than “Before” in most cases, indicating a modest mitigation effect, though not universally significant.
